recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: SD-070 P0a trains split_encoder.world_encoder on RAW world_state, but agent.sense() reads it through the never-trained world_obs_encoder pre-projection -- train/inference path divergence costing ~0.10 absolute decodability on the pathway E1/E2/E3 actually read
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: ZWorldP0Trainer._z_world_path (ree_core/latent/zworld_p0.py) trains `split_encoder.world_encoder` directly on RAW `world_state`. Production inference (`REEAgent.sense`, ree_core/agent.py) instead feeds `world_state` through `agent.world_obs_encoder` -- a separately-initialised Linear+ReLU -- and only then into `split_encoder.world_encoder`. The encoder is therefore trained on one input distribution and evaluated on another. Work needed: make the two paths agree -- either train P0a THROUGH `world_obs_encoder` (so the recipe optimises the production path), or bypass `world_obs_encoder` at inference for the z_world path (so production reads the path P0a trained), or train `world_obs_encoder` as part of the P0a recipe. Choosing between them is the build decision and needs the owner of SD-070; all three are `complicated (buildable)`. NOTE the migration cost the 1030 driver's own red-team F5a flagged and which is the reason this was left alone until now: changing the recipe re-touches every driver that depends on it, so the entry should be scheduled, not hot-patched.
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.severity_rationale: DELIBERATELY `degrading`, NOT `corrupting`, and the distinction is load-bearing because of blast radius. `corrupting` means a new experiment touching `substrate_paths` is STOP-gated by /queue-experiment Step 2.5c, which matches at MODULE granularity -- and `ree_core/agent.py` is entered by essentially every REE driver, so a `corrupting` stamp here would gate the entire experiment programme, including the repair this autopsy routes and the sibling H1 leg. That asymmetry is the same one the confirmed failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-1004_2026-09-05 reasoned through for causal_grid_world.py. On the merits `degrading` is also the correct classification: the pre-projection does not make a metric read as a clean null that is secretly invalid -- it uniformly ATTENUATES decodability on the sense() path, and for a question about what the PRODUCTION path carries, measuring through the production path is correct rather than corrupting. What is defective is that the TRAINING path and the INFERENCE path diverge, which degrades what the encoder can deliver and weakens confidence in any z_world-readout magnitude.

learning_extracted: R3 IS A MIS-SPECIFIED POSITIVE CONTROL -- the load-bearing finding. R3 `zworld_probe_extracts_known_signal` decodes the agent's absolute grid QUADRANT (from env.agent_x / env.agent_y) out of z_world, on the driver's stated premise that 'agent position is reflected in the local view' (driver `_quadrant_label` docstring, line 420ff). That premise is FALSE, and the environment source says so verbatim: `CausalGridWorldV2._get_observation_dict` puts agent_x/size and agent_y/size in body_state[0] and body_state[1], while world_state is composed exclusively of AGENT-CENTRED 5x5 windows -- local_view (5x5x7 = 175), contamination_view (25), hazard_field_view (25), resource_field_view (25), waypoint_proximity_field_view (25) = 275. z_world is computed from world_state alone (`split_encoder.world_encoder(world_state)`; the driver's own `_direct_zworld` confirms it). Absolute position is therefore reachable from world_state only through (a) the out-of-bounds zero-padding pattern when the agent is within 2 cells of a wall -- the env is non-toroidal by default, but on a 12x12 grid roughly 44% of cells (the interior 8x8) carry no boundary cue at all -- and (b) episode-specific hazard/resource layout, which an EPISODE-LEVEL train/test split deliberately makes non-generalising. So R3 tests a signal that is weakly, non-uniformly and partly non-generalisably present, not one that 'must be decodable if the probe pipeline can extract anything at this scale at all'. The manifest carries the fingerprint: quadrant TRAIN accuracy is 0.521-0.612 in all 10 cells, i.e. the probe cannot fit the supposedly-present signal even on its own training data, and on seed 43 test accuracy (0.762) EXCEEDS train accuracy (0.521) by 0.24 -- a statistic driven by which 8 episodes landed in the test split, not by competence.

THE R3 DEFECT DOES NOT FLIP THE VERDICT TO 'C1 MET / H2 SUPPORTED', AND THIS IS THE TRAP. With R3 invalidated it is tempting to read C1's own cells (4 of 5 seeds inside the +/-0.05 null band, required 3) as a clean PASS. It is not, because invalidating R3 removes the guard without removing the hazard it was built for: red-team F1 on this driver named exactly the failure mode of an under-fit or scale-starved z_world probe reading OFF ~ ON ~ majority-class in both arms and satisfying C1's null BY CONSTRUCTION. The manifest shows that hazard REALISED. The z_world probe's held-out accuracy is at or BELOW its own test majority-class rate in 6 of 10 cells (seed 44 OFF 0.230 vs 0.498; seed 44 ON 0.350 vs 0.498; seed 45 OFF 0.401 vs 0.463; seed 45 ON 0.381 vs 0.463; seed 46 OFF 0.416 vs 0.518; seed 46 ON 0.458 vs 0.518), and clears it materially in only 2 (seed 42 OFF +0.171, ON +0.140). A near-zero difference between two sub-majority numbers is not a measured null. The correct verdict is that the run is uninterpretable -- which is what the driver self-routed, arriving at the right answer via a control that could not have told it so.

THE FITTING BUDGET IS NOT SCALE-MATCHED ACROSS THE FEATURE SPACES IT IS COMPARED OVER. All four probes share `PROBE_STEPS = 150` full-batch Adam steps at `PROBE_LR = 5e-3` on UNSTANDARDISED features, but the raw probe reads a 25/50-dim slice bounded in [0,1] while the z_world probes read a 32-dim 0.9-EMA latent whose scale is set by `world_precision_logit` and whatever P0a left. The consequence is visible: the raw ON-arm probe reaches train accuracy 0.743-0.828 under that budget, while the sense()-path DV probe tops out at 0.487-0.576 train and the R3 quadrant probe at 0.521-0.612 (the direct-path probe reaches 0.539-0.692 -- higher, and the reason the range is quoted per probe rather than as one 'z_world-path' band). A comparison whose positive control is fit to 0.83 and whose DV is fit to 0.52 is not controlled for fitting adequacy, whatever it reports.

A PRECONDITION GATE CAN MAKE A CRITERION'S OWN CELLS READ 'MET' WHILE THE FLAG READS false, AND NOTHING WARNS THE READER. `criteria.C1_zworld_lift_null` in this manifest reads `met: false` next to `measured: 0.8, threshold: 0.6, n_seeds_met: 4, required_seeds: 3` -- because `_score` computes `c1 = measurable and (len(null_seeds) >= need)` and folds the R3 precondition into the criterion boolean while the criterion's reported cells are computed independently of it. Any downstream reader (human or index) that compares measured against threshold gets the opposite answer from the flag. The repair is cheap and worth generalising: when a precondition suppresses a criterion, emit the suppression explicitly on the criterion block (`suppressed_by: <precondition name>`) rather than only flipping `met`.

FIRST QUANTIFIED COST OF THE SD-070 `agent.sense()` PRE-PROJECTION (driver red-team F5a). The `zworld_direct_probe` -- which mirrors `_z_world_path` exactly and bypasses `agent.world_obs_encoder` -- outperforms the sense()-path probe on the identical label, identical episode split, identical fitting budget and identical frozen encoder in 8 of 10 cells: means 0.4838 vs 0.3832 (OFF, +0.1006) and 0.5086 vs 0.4023 (ON, +0.1063). This is a paired within-cell contrast and is the strongest evidence yet that the untrained pre-projection destroys real information before the trained encoder ever sees it, on the pathway every production consumer (E1/E2/E3) actually reads. SCOPE THE CLAIM CORRECTLY (Step 7c red-team F1): it is NOT true that 'nothing in the corpus ever trains' world_obs_encoder -- 85 drivers build an optimiser over `agent.parameters()`, which includes it. The true claim is lineage-scoped: 0 of the 34 drivers calling `run_zworld_p0` train it, so within the SD-070 P0a lineage the training path (`_z_world_path`, raw world_state) and the inference path (`sense()`, via the pre-projection) diverge with nothing reconciling them. Two caveats keep this from being a verdict: the direct path has no known-signal anchor of its own in this run either, and BOTH paths show a near-null ON-OFF lift (direct-path per-seed lifts -0.003, +0.044, +0.072, 0.000, +0.012), so this locates an absolute information loss, not the specific loss of the waypoint gradient. It is now tracked: recommended_substrate_queue_entry action `create`, severity `degrading`.

THE `p0a_holdout` BLOCK IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE POSITIVE CONTROL, THOUGH IT LOOKS LIKE ONE. Across all 40 (cell x head) readings it reports balanced accuracies of 0.9869-1.0000 with mean_lift ~0.58 on hazard_present / resource_present / hazard_distance / resource_distance -- tempting to cite as proof that z_world is richly informative and therefore that the probe must be the limiter. It cannot carry that weight: `ZWorldP0Trainer._holdout_report` splits with a FLAT `torch.randperm` over samples, not by episode, so it is exposed to precisely the within-episode near-duplicate leakage that red-team F4 made this driver's own probes split by episode to avoid; and it reads `_z_world_path` (the direct path) through the trainer's OWN heads, not the sense() features the DV uses. Its label balance also makes the raw number flattering -- see item 11. What it does establish is narrower and still useful: the z_world path is not collapsed or degenerate.

THE PAIRED-ENV DESIGN WORKED AND SHOULD BE KEPT. `_FieldMaskedEnv` (red-team F2) always builds the wide field-enabled env and zeroes the trailing 25 world_state columns under OFF. The manifest confirms it end to end: `label_counts` is byte-identical across arms within every seed (e.g. seed 42: 359/289/269/223/0 in both), `world_obs_dim` is 275 in both arms, and `field_cols_weight_delta` is EXACTLY 0.0 in all five OFF cells (a masked-to-zero input column receives exactly zero gradient) against 2.018-2.160 in all five ON cells. The ON/OFF contrast is genuinely paired at the trajectory level. A per-column reading of the ON deltas is worth recording for the next iteration: the 25 field columns move with norm ~2.09 against ~11.0 for the other 250, i.e. about 0.19 of the other block's norm where an iid per-column expectation would give sqrt(25/250) ~ 0.32 -- suggestive that P0a moves the field columns LESS than the rest, consistent with an untasked channel, but a norm ratio is not a per-column effect size and this must not be read as a measurement.

THE C0 POSITIVE CONTROL STANDS, BUT ITS OFF ARM IS SUB-TRIVIAL AND THAT SHOULD BE SAID. C0 met 5/5 (per-seed raw lift 0.214-0.424 against a 0.15 floor) and replicates V3-EXQ-1004's input-level finding. Note for the record that the OFF-arm raw probe sits BELOW its own test majority-class rate on 4 of 5 seeds (0.353 vs 0.507; 0.250 vs 0.413; 0.231 vs 0.346; 0.467 vs 0.513), so part of the lift is an OFF-arm floor rather than pure ON-arm signal. The control survives it: the ON arm clears majority on all 5 seeds by +0.131 to +0.267, so the direction and the magnitude are carried by real ON-arm information.

A POSITIVE CONTROL CAN FAIL IN EITHER DIRECTION, AND THE SECOND DIRECTION IS THE EASIER MISTAKE. R3 as built could never pass (its target is not in the feature space it certifies -- item 1). The FIRST DRAFT of this autopsy's own repair recommendation would have installed the mirror-image defect: replace R3's target with a P0a scene-structure label but keep an ABSOLUTE floor. The manifest's own `p0a_grounding_label_balance` shows why that is unfailable -- hazard_distance [0.0, 0.078, 0.197, 0.725] and resource_distance [0.0, 0.115, 0.241, 0.645], bucket 0 carrying exactly zero mass, so a constant-majority predictor scores 0.725 / 0.645 and clears any 0.55-style floor in every cell without decoding anything. Caught by the Step 7c red-team, not by the 7b mechanical checks, which have no view of label balance. The generalisable rule: a readiness threshold on an imbalanced label must be stated relative to that cell's own realised majority-class rate, never as an absolute accuracy. This is a candidate for a standing lint (see recommended_substrate_queue_entry.governance_also_to_decide).

CORRECTION TO THIS AUTOPSY'S OWN FIRST-DRAFT MECHANISM STORY, recorded rather than silently fixed (Step 7c red-team, hygiene). The draft said absolute position could leak into world_state near walls via 'out-of-bounds ZERO-PADDING'. The local view does not zero-pad out-of-bounds cells: it marks them with a one-hot `wall` entity channel. required_changes: REPLACE R3's target AND ITS THRESHOLD FORM -- both halves are required (Step 7c red-team F2 on the first draft, which specified only the target). (a) TARGET: the positive control must read a label genuinely present in world_state and generalising ACROSS episodes. The natural family is the SD-018/SD-070 P0a scene-structure targets (`scene_structure_targets`: hazard_present / resource_present / hazard_distance / resource_distance), carried by the hazard_field_view / resource_field_view windows in world_state by construction and the very content P0a optimises. (b) THRESHOLD: it must be MAJORITY-RELATIVE, never an absolute floor. Those labels are severely imbalanced and this run's own manifest proves it -- `p0a_grounding_label_balance` reads hazard_distance [0.0, 0.078, 0.197, 0.725] and resource_distance [0.0, 0.115, 0.241, 0.645] (bucket 0 carries EXACTLY ZERO mass in both). A constant-majority predictor therefore scores 0.725 / 0.645 on those labels and would clear a 0.55-style absolute floor in every cell without decoding anything -- an unfailable positive control by construction, which is the same defect class as the R3 being replaced, merely inverted (R3 could never pass; this would never fail). Require a declared margin OVER the cell's own realised majority-class rate, exactly as change [4] already requires for the DV. Keep the quadrant probe as a NON-load-bearing diagnostic if desired; it must not gate anything.

MEASURE R3 THROUGH THE SAME PIPELINE AS THE DV -- same sense()-path z_world features, same episode-level split, same fitting budget, same seeds. Otherwise the control certifies a different procedure from the one under test. This is exactly why the existing p0a_holdout block cannot stand in for it (it splits flat, not by episode, and reads the direct path through the trainer's own heads).

SCALE-MATCH THE FITTING. Standardise features per probe (or fit to a convergence criterion with per-space early stopping) and report each probe's TRAIN accuracy as a first-class readiness number alongside its held-out accuracy, so 'the positive control was fit to 0.83 while the DV was fit to 0.52' can never again pass unremarked.

ADD A DV-FLOOR READINESS CHECK. Require the z_world probe to clear ITS OWN test majority-class rate by a declared margin in a declared fraction of cells BEFORE the ON-OFF null is read at all. This is the check that would have caught the realised F1 hazard directly rather than by proxy, and its absence is why the run had to lean on the mis-specified R3.

DECIDE AND DECLARE THE STATUS OF THE DIRECT PATH (Step 7c red-team F3). The sense()-path DV is the right primary readout -- it is the pathway production consumers read. But on the DIRECT path, seeds 42, 43 and 46 clear their own majority-class rate in BOTH arms with ON-OFF lifts of -0.003, +0.044 and +0.012, i.e. a DV-floor check like [4] would be SATISFIED on the direct path at 3 of 5 seeds and C1's null would then be met at 3/3 of the qualifying seeds. That is not a verdict on this run (the direct path has no known-signal anchor here either, and the pre-registered DV is the sense() path), but 1030a must say up front whether the direct path is CO-PRIMARY with its own criterion or stays a diagnostic -- deciding it after seeing the numbers is the thing to avoid.
